rationale: The DELTA(ppent/ppegt) renewal leg has already been tested against three separate distress conditioners in the archive (Distressed Asset Renewal Surge, Renewal Funding Shortfall, Renewal Payoff Failure), so swapping in a fourth cash-and-maturity conditioner is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

This is Maturity-Wall Capex Acceleration with the dlc/lt level replaced by its one-year change — a minimal level-to-change tweak that also compounds a noisy second difference (ACCEL) with a noisy first difference, making it more likely to weaken than clarify the archived result.

The five-year TREND in inventory-to-sales is a genuinely different construct from the level, delta, and volatility versions already archived, and the credit-fragility conditioner is economically coherent, though the NEG(che/at) component overlaps with Supplier-Financed Inventory Build and the long window will cut coverage.

This is a recombination of two archived signals — the collateral-mix denominator from Soft-Asset Collateral Shift and the dlc/lt conditioner from Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility, with NEG(ceq/at) substituted for NEG(oancf/at) — and since dlc/lt and low ceq/at are both leverage proxies the conditioner is largely redundant; the interaction_type label "ratio" is also inconsistent with what is plainly a conditional interaction.

Directly rediscovers Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend with only one of two conditioner components swapped (lct/act to NEG(ceq/at), NEG(oancf/at) retained), in a channel already mined six ways in the archive, and the underlying acquirer-underperformance-times-distress effect is close to published anomaly territory.

Shifting from labor-growth flows to the industry-relative level of employee intensity is a real change in the base variable rather than a cosmetic tweak and the fixed-cost-plus-rollover-risk logic is internally consistent, but emp/sale is the inverse of the well-studied sales-per-employee productivity signal, so the novelty rests entirely on the conditioning interaction.
